In [[differential geometry]], a '''Wente torus''' is an [[immersion (mathematics)|immersed]] [[torus]] in <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math> of constant [[mean curvature]], discovered by {{harvs|first=Henry C.|last=Wente|authorlink=Henry C. Wente|year=1986|txt}}.  It is a counterexample to the conjecture of [[Heinz Hopf]] that every [[closed manifold|closed]], [[compact space|compact]], [[constant-mean-curvature surface]] is a [[sphere]] (though this is true if the surface is [[embedding|embedded]]).  There are similar examples known for every positive [[genus (mathematics)|genus]].
